items.title: Hadamard character sum on F_2^n
items.statement_or_definition:
For $n\ge1$ and $z\in\{0,1\}^n$, with the binary dot product of [[def-qa-binary-dot-product]],
$$
\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}(-1)^{x\cdot z}=\begin{cases}2^n,&z=0^n,\\0,&z\ne0^n.\end{cases}
$$
Consequently, for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$,
$$
H^{\otimes n}|x\rangle=2^{-n/2}\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^n}(-1)^{x\cdot y}|y\rangle,
$$
where $H$ is the exact one-qubit gate of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and tensor factors follow the ordered register convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]].
proof_obligations: Factor the finite sum into ∏_i Σ_{x_i∈{0,1}}(-1)^{x_i z_i}; state tensor order and normalization.

items.title: Deutsch constant-versus-balanced promise
items.statement_or_definition: Let $f:\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}$ be the total Boolean function of a [[def-qa-promise-query-instance]]. The **Deutsch promise** is the decision task with YES set $Y=\{f:f(0)=f(1)\}$ and NO set $N=\{f:f(0)\ne f(1)\}$. The required output is $0$ on $Y$ (constant) and $1$ on $N$ (balanced). All four Boolean functions on one bit are promised.
proof_obligations: Check the four truth tables partition into two constant and two balanced cases.

items.title: Deutsch–Jozsa promise
items.statement_or_definition: Let $n\ge1$, let $N:=2^n$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be the total function of a [[def-qa-promise-query-instance]]. The **Deutsch–Jozsa promise** is the decision task with YES set consisting of constant functions and NO set consisting of functions taking each value $0$ and $1$ exactly $N/2$ times. The required output is constant or balanced, respectively. Here $n$ is the address width, and $N$ is the number of addresses, as supplied by [[thm-qc-bitstring-index-is-bijection]] and [[def-finite-cardinality]]. Encode an instance by its $N$-bit truth table in lexicographic address order; its encoded input size is therefore $N$, not $n$, under [[def-qa-input-encoding-and-size]]. In the query-instance convention, the length-$N$ family has address width $a(N)=n$ and reply width $b(N)=1$; the public parameter $n$ determines the registers, while the unknown truth table is supplied through oracle queries. Lengths that are not powers of two at least two have empty promise.
proof_obligations: Verify the two promise sets are disjoint and state n≥1 so the balanced class is meaningful.

items.title: Bernstein–Vazirani no-offset promise
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $n\ge1$. The **Bernstein–Vazirani no-offset promise** consists of the total functions
$$
f_a:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\},\qquad f_a(x):=a\cdot x,
$$
for an unknown secret $a\in\{0,1\}^n$, using [[def-qa-binary-dot-product]]. The task is to output $a$. This version has no additive offset: the oracle is exactly $f_a$, not $x\mapsto a\cdot x\oplus b$.
proof_obligations: State whether the query function is total and verify the secret a is uniquely determined by its values.

items.title: One classical query cannot solve Deutsch exactly
items.statement_or_definition: On the Deutsch promise, the exact deterministic classical query complexity is $2$. Every randomized classical algorithm making at most one query has worst-case success probability at most $1/2$ under per-input correctness.
proof_obligations: For either first query address, pair a constant oracle with a balanced oracle agreeing at that address; use their indistinguishable transcripts.

items.title: Exact deterministic Deutsch–Jozsa needs N/2+1 queries
items.statement_or_definition: For $n\ge1$ and $N=2^n$, the exact deterministic classical query complexity of the Deutsch–Jozsa promise is $N/2+1$.
proof_obligations: Construct a balanced completion of the all-zero transcript for any set of at most N/2 queried points.

items.title: Three classical samples solve Deutsch–Jozsa with bounded error
items.statement_or_definition: For $n\ge2$, the finite probability experiment that samples three distinct addresses uniformly without replacement and outputs constant exactly when all three replies agree has success probability at least $3/4$ on every Deutsch–Jozsa input. In the finite fair-bit classical query model, sampling three independent uniform addresses with replacement and using the same output rule also succeeds with probability at least $3/4$, using exactly $3n$ random bits and three value queries. For $n=1$, querying both addresses solves the promise exactly with two queries. Thus the deterministic exact lower bound is not a bounded-error exponential separation.
proof_obligations: Compute the without-replacement probability and handle N=2 separately; state that this bounded-error upper bound means the exact deterministic separation is not a bounded-error exponential separation.

items.title: Classical Bernstein–Vazirani needs n queries for bounded error
items.statement_or_definition: For the no-offset Bernstein–Vazirani promise on $n\ge1$ bits, every randomized classical algorithm with worst-case success at least $2/3$ needs at least $n$ queries. Querying the $n$ standard basis addresses recovers the secret exactly, so the bounded-error and exact classical query complexities are both $n$.
proof_obligations: Formalize adaptive decision-tree leaves and average over the 2^n secrets; distinguish query cost from bit-processing cost.

items.title: One-query Deutsch algorithm
items.statement_or_definition:
**Input.** A one-bit total Boolean oracle $f$ satisfying the Deutsch promise of [[def-qa-deutsch-promise]], with an address qubit $A$ and target qubit $T$ initialized to $|0\rangle_A|0\rangle_T$.

**Output.** One classical bit: output $0$ for constant and $1$ for balanced.

**Gate model.** The declared nonoracle gate alphabet permits exact callable $H$ and $X$ gates, each occurrence charged as one nonoracle gate under [[def-qa-nonoracle-gate-cost]]. The supplied standard bit query is charged separately as one oracle call.

**Procedure.** Apply $X$ to $T$, then apply $H$ to $T$ and $H$ to $A$. Invoke the standard XOR oracle $U_f$ once on the ordered pair $(A,T)$. Apply $H$ to $A$, measure $A$ in its ordered computational basis, and output the measured bit. There are no intermediate measurements, loops, or failure branches.

The terminal measurement is specified by [[def-qa-finite-branch-output-law]] and is separate from the declared one-qubit gate resource. No circuit-uniformity or classical bit-time bound is asserted.

The standard bit query and its controlled-access conventions are those of [[def-qa-standard-bit-query]] and [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]]. The one-query phase action used by this procedure is verified by [[thm-qa-bit-query-to-phase-query]].
proof_obligations: Specify zero initialization, ordered registers, exact X/H instructions, the single oracle invocation and terminal output rule; resource totals are proved in thm-qa-deutsch-query-correct.

items.title: One-query Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm
items.statement_or_definition:
**Input.** An integer $n\ge1$ and a total Boolean oracle $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ satisfying the Deutsch–Jozsa promise of [[def-qa-deutsch-jozsa-promise]], with an ordered $n$-qubit address register $A$ and one target qubit $T$ initialized to $|0^n\rangle_A|0\rangle_T$.

**Output.** One classical bit: output $0$ (constant) exactly when the measured address is $0^n$; otherwise output $1$ (balanced).

**Gate model.** The declared nonoracle gate alphabet permits exact callable $H$ and $X$ gates, each occurrence charged as one nonoracle gate under [[def-qa-nonoracle-gate-cost]]. The supplied standard bit query is charged separately as one oracle call.

**Procedure.** Apply $H^{\otimes n}$ to $A$. Apply $X$ and then $H$ to $T$. Invoke the standard XOR oracle $U_f$ once on $(A,T)$. Apply $H^{\otimes n}$ to $A$, measure $A$ in its ordered computational basis, and apply the output rule. There are no intermediate measurements, loops, or failure branches.

The terminal measurement is specified by [[def-qa-finite-branch-output-law]] and is separate from the declared one-qubit gate resource. No circuit-uniformity or classical bit-time bound is asserted.

The standard XOR query and quantum-query algorithm conventions are those of [[def-qa-standard-bit-query]] and [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]]. The phase action used by the procedure is verified by [[thm-qa-bit-query-to-phase-query]].
proof_obligations: Specify zero initialization, ordered registers, exact X/H instructions, the single oracle invocation and terminal output rule; resource totals are proved in thm-qa-deutsch-jozsa-query-correct.

items.title: One-query Bernstein–Vazirani algorithm
items.statement_or_definition:
**Input.** An integer $n\ge1$ and an oracle $f_a(x)=a\cdot x$ satisfying the no-offset Bernstein–Vazirani promise of [[def-qa-bernstein-vazirani-promise]], on an ordered $n$-qubit address register $A$ and one target qubit $T$ initialized to $|0^n\rangle_A|0\rangle_T$.

**Output.** The measured $n$-bit address, interpreted as the secret $a$.

**Gate model.** The declared nonoracle gate alphabet permits exact callable $H$ and $X$ gates, each occurrence charged as one nonoracle gate under [[def-qa-nonoracle-gate-cost]]. The supplied standard bit query is charged separately as one oracle call.

**Procedure.** Apply $H^{\otimes n}$ to $A$. Apply $X$ and then $H$ to $T$. Invoke the standard XOR oracle $U_{f_a}$ once on $(A,T)$. Apply $H^{\otimes n}$ to $A$, measure $A$ in its ordered computational basis, and output the measured string. There are no intermediate measurements, loops, or failure branches.

The terminal measurement is specified by [[def-qa-finite-branch-output-law]] and is separate from the declared one-qubit gate resource. No circuit-uniformity or classical bit-time bound is asserted.

The standard XOR query and quantum-query algorithm conventions are those of [[def-qa-standard-bit-query]] and [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]]. The phase action used by the procedure is verified by [[thm-qa-bit-query-to-phase-query]].
proof_obligations: Specify zero initialization, ordered registers, exact X/H instructions, the single oracle invocation and terminal output rule; resource totals are proved in thm-qa-bernstein-vazirani-query-correct.

items.title: Deutsch algorithm is exact
items.statement_or_definition: For either promised one-bit function $f$, the final measurement of [[alg-qa-deutsch-query]] outputs $0$ with probability one when $f$ is constant and $1$ with probability one when $f$ is balanced. In the algorithm's declared exact $X,H$ gate model, it uses exactly one oracle query and one $X$ and three $H$ gates, totaling four one-qubit gates. The terminal measurement is a separate resource.
proof_obligations: Evaluate the phase state and the final two-term Hadamard transform in both promise cases.
Count the single oracle call and all X/H occurrences in the declared gate model; report terminal measurement separately.

items.title: Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm is exact
items.statement_or_definition: For every $n\ge1$ and every function satisfying the Deutsch–Jozsa promise, [[alg-qa-deutsch-jozsa-query]] outputs constant with probability one on constant inputs and balanced with probability one on balanced inputs. In the algorithm's declared exact $X,H$ gate model, it uses exactly one oracle query and one $X$ and $2n+1$ $H$ gates, totaling $2n+2$ one-qubit gates. The terminal measurement is a separate resource.
proof_obligations: Use the exact y=0 amplitude 2^{-n}Σ_x(-1)^{f(x)} and balance promise.

items.title: Bernstein–Vazirani algorithm returns the secret exactly
